Otti, who disclosed this during his monthly media conference at the weekend in Umuahia, the state capital, stressed that details of the ongoing negotiations would not be made public.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.summary_zh: 阿比亚州州长亚历克斯·奥蒂博士表示，东南部各州州长仍未放弃争取释放被拘留的比亚法拉原住民领导人马齐·南南迪·卡努的努力，并坚称他们仍在幕后与相关联邦当局接洽。奥蒂在周末于州首府乌穆阿比亚举行的每月媒体会议上透露了这一消息，并强调，正在进行的谈判细节不会对外公布。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.body: Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, has stated that the South-east governors had not abandoned efforts to secure the release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, insisting they were still engaging relevant federal authorities behind the scenes. Otti, who disclosed this during his monthly media conference at the weekend in Umuahia, the state capital, stressed that details of the ongoing negotiations would not be made public. Kanu is serving a life sentence following his conviction on terrorism-related charges by the Federal High Court, Abuja. Meanwhile, the governor also disclosed that Abia’s debt profile had dropped from ₦147.2 billion in the second quarter of 2023 to ₦48.6 billion in the second quarter of 2026, representing a reduction of ₦98.6 billion. Addressing concerns over rising foreign debt obligations, Otti explained that the increase reflected drawdowns from existing multilateral facilities, including the Abia State Integrated Infrastructure Development Project (ABSIID) and the Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project (RAAMP). He maintained that his administration had undertaken no direct borrowing, adding that any future loans would be strictly tied to productive investments. “We will borrow for regenerative projects at the right time,” he said. The governor also announced that the CKC water scheme in Aba was ready for commissioning, expressing optimism that residents would soon enjoy improved access to public water supply. He disclosed that another smart school would also be commissioned, bringing the number planned for the state to 21 following approvals for an additional facility. Otti said his administration was working to standardise education in public and private schools, adding that a committee set up to assess government interventions had recommended measures to promote healthy competition and improve standards. The governor further disclosed that Abia ranked second in the 2025/2026 Climate Governance Ranking, while over 5,000 Certificates of Occupancy had been issued in three years. On public health, Otti said the state had activated precautionary measures following Nigeria’s Ebola index case, with an isolation centre designated at the Modern Child Hospital. He, however, stressed that no Ebola case had been recorded in Abia, urging residents to remain calm while observing health protocols. On eye care services, Otti disclosed that over 31,000 screening exercises had been conducted and 1,811 patients operated on, including 304 beneficiaries of free cataract surgeries for vulnerable residents. He commended the Eye Care Management Bureau for its efforts, promising to invest more in providing quality eyecare services to the people. Otti also encourages residents to go for eye screening, stressing that early detection of eye ailments helps in preventing blindness. On the planned relocation of traders around Isi-Gate in Umuahia, Otti said the exercise would be gradual, insisting that affected traders must be provided alternatives to protect their livelihoods. He also directed that the ₦1 billion personal gift announced for teachers during the 2026 World Teachers’ Day be shared among all teachers in the state, irrespective of rank or position. He clarified that the money was a personal gift and not an official government programme or promotion-related benefit. Otti said his administration had prioritised road projects according to economic importance and urgency, with major roads in Aba and Umuahia receiving attention because of their impact on businesses, mobility, employment and revenue generation. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.body_zh: 阿比亚州州长亚历克斯·奥蒂博士表示，东南部各州州长并未放弃争取获释被拘留的比夫拉原住民组织（IPOB）领袖马齐·南南迪·卡努的努力，并强调他们仍在幕后与相关联邦当局进行交涉。奥蒂于周末在州首府乌穆阿希亚举行的每月媒体会议上披露了此事，并强调正在进行的谈判细节不会公开。卡努因联邦高等法院判决其犯有与恐怖主义有关的罪行，目前正在服终身刑。与此同时，该州长还透露，阿比亚州的债务规模已从2023年第二季度的1472亿奈拉降至2026年第二季度的486亿奈拉，减少了986亿奈拉。针对外国债务偿付义务上升的担忧，奥蒂解释说，这一增长反映了对现有多边融资安排的提款，其中包括阿比亚州综合基础设施发展项目（ABSIID）和农村通道与农业营销项目（RAAMP）。他坚称本届政府没有进行任何直接借款，并表示今后的任何贷款都将严格用于生产性投资。他说：“我们会在适当的时候为促进再生型项目融资。”州长还宣布，位于阿巴的CKC供水项目已具备启用条件，并乐观表示，居民很快将能更好地获得公共供水。他透露，另一所智能学校也将投入使用；在为增建设施获批后，该州计划建设的此类学校数量将达到21所。奥蒂表示，本届政府正致力于推动公立和私立学校的教育标准化，并补充说，一个为评估政府干预措施而成立的委员会建议采取相关措施，以促进良性竞争并提高教学标准。州长进一步透露，阿比亚州在2025/2026年气候治理排名中位居第二；三年间已签发5000多份占用证书。在公共卫生方面，奥蒂表示，尼日利亚出现首例埃博拉指数病例后，该州已启动预防措施，并在现代儿童医院指定设立隔离中心。不过，他强调阿比亚州尚未发现埃博拉病例，同时敦促居民保持冷静并遵守卫生规程。在眼科服务方面，奥蒂透露，已开展3.1万多例筛查，并为1811名患者实施手术，其中包括为弱势居民免费实施白内障手术的304名受益者。他称赞了眼科护理管理局所做的工作，并承诺进一步投资，为民众提供优质眼科服务。奥蒂还鼓励居民接受眼科筛查，强调及早发现眼病有助于预防失明。关于乌穆阿希亚Isi-Gate周边商贩的搬迁计划，奥蒂表示，搬迁将逐步进行，并坚持必须为受影响商贩提供替代方案，以保障其生计。他还指示，在2026年世界教师节期间宣布向教师赠送的10亿奈拉个人礼物，应在全州所有教师之间分配，不论其职级或职位。他澄清，这笔钱是个人赠送，而非政府官方项目或与晋升有关的福利。奥蒂表示，本届政府根据经济重要性和紧迫性确定道路项目的优先次序，阿巴和乌穆阿希亚的主要道路因对商业、出行、就业和创收具有重要影响而受到重视。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕Creek Road 35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。该报是尼日利亚面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛中产阶级的权威新闻媒体，服务于所有平台，同时充当有抱负者和千禧一代探索新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。作为一份致力于追求真相与理性的公共信托报纸，该报报道范围广泛，涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区议题，直至人与社会的交汇领域。您可以发送邮件至hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/a.title: Adegbuyi Urges Geographic Audit of Nigeria’s Voters’ Register
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/a.summary: A former Postmaster-General of the Federation and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST), Bisi Adegbuyi, has called for an independent technical review of Nigeria’s voters’ register. Adegbuyi said the review should go beyond establishing voter identity to examine the geographic accuracy, consistency and verifiability of registration records.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/a.summary_zh: 尼日利亚联邦前邮电总监、尼日利亚邮政（NIPOST）首席执行官比西·阿德格布伊呼吁对尼日利亚选民登记册进行独立技术审查。阿德格布伊表示，审查不应仅限于确认选民身份，还应检验登记记录的地理准确性、一致性和可核查性。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/a.body: A former Postmaster-General of the Federation and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST), Bisi Adegbuyi, has called for an independent technical review of Nigeria’s voters’ register. Adegbuyi said the review should go beyond establishing voter identity to examine the geographic accuracy, consistency and verifiability of registration records. He made the call in a statement against the backdrop of recent concerns over the integrity of the voters’ register and questions surrounding some voter records. According to him, credible elections require attention not only to how election results are transmitted, but also to the accuracy of the geographic information attached to voter registrations. Adegbuyi recalled that he had proposed a technical framework on February 27, 2026, for modernising legacy voter addresses without disrupting existing electoral arrangements. The proposal recommended the use of machine-assisted interpretation, geographic resolution and deterministic digital location referencing to improve the quality of voter-location data. He said the approach could help electoral administrators identify inconsistencies, detect unusual geographic concentrations and strengthen the auditability of polling-unit assignments. Adegbuyi stressed that the proposed framework would not require replacing Permanent Voter Cards or the existing biometric verification system. Instead, he said, geographic verification would provide an additional layer of assurance alongside existing identity and biometric checks. His renewed proposal comes amid recent concerns about questionable voter photographs and possible procedural lapses in the management of voter information. Adegbuyi acknowledged that geographic verification alone could not resolve all questions relating to voter identity or data integrity. However, he argued that it could complement existing verification mechanisms and provide another means of identifying inconsistencies within the register. “Nigeria’s electoral infrastructure deserves a verification framework in which identity, geography, provenance and accountability reinforce one another,” he said. The former NIPOST chief urged relevant authorities to subject his earlier recommendations to an independent technical assessment. He stressed that any review or implementation should remain subject to electoral laws, data-protection requirements and the statutory authority of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Adegbuyi said the objective should be to strengthen the reliability of the electoral register without undermining existing voter-identification arrangements. He argued that the credibility of the register depends not only on establishing who is registered, but also on verifying whether the information associated with each registration is accurate and consistent. “The credibility of a voters’ register depends not only on who is registered, but also on whether the information associated with each registration is accurate, consistent and verifiable,” he said. Adegbuyi’s proposal places geographic information alongside identity and biometric data as part of a broader framework for strengthening Nigeria’s electoral infrastructure. The approach would, among other things, provide electoral administrators with additional tools for examining voter-location patterns and identifying records requiring further scrutiny. He said the current concerns surrounding the register provided an opportunity to revisit technical approaches that could improve verification and accountability before future elections. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/a.title_zh: 阿德格布伊敦促对尼日利亚选民登记册进行地理审核
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/a.body_zh: 尼日利亚联邦前邮政总局局长兼尼日利亚邮政局（NIPOST）首席执行官Bisi Adegbuyi呼吁对尼日利亚选民登记册进行独立技术审查。Adegbuyi表示，审查不应仅限于确认选民身份，还应考察登记记录的地理准确性、一致性和可核验性。鉴于近期有关选民登记册完整性的担忧，以及部分选民记录引发的疑问，他在一份声明中提出这一呼吁。据他可信的选举不仅需要关注选举结果如何传输，也需要关注选民登记所附地理信息的准确性。Adegbuyi回忆称，他曾于2026年2月27日提出一套技术框架，在不扰乱现有选举安排的情况下实现遗留选民地址的现代化。该建议主张采用机器辅助判读、地理解析和确定性数字位置引用，以提升选民位置数据的质量。他说，这一方法可以帮助选举管理人员识别不一致之处、发现异常地理集中现象，并加强对投票站分配的审计能力。Adegbuyi强调，拟议框架不要求更换永久选民卡或现有生物特征核验系统。相反，他说，地理核验将在现有身份核验和生物特征核验之外提供一层额外保障。他重新提出这项建议之际，近期外界对部分选民照片的可信度以及选民信息管理中可能存在的程序疏失表示担忧。Adegbuyi承认，仅靠地理核验无法解决所有与选民身份或数据完整性有关的问题。然而他认为，地理核验可以补充现有核验机制，并为识别登记册中的不一致情况提供另一种手段。他说：“尼日利亚的选举基础设施应当拥有一套核验框架，使身份、地理、来源和问责机制相互印证。”这位尼日利亚邮政局前负责人敦促有关当局对他先前提出的建议进行独立技术评估。他强调，任何审查或实施工作都应遵守选举法律、数据保护要求以及独立国家选举委员会（INEC）的法定权限。Adegbuyi表示，目标是提高选民登记册的可靠性，同时不削弱现有选民身份识别安排。他认为，登记册的可信度不仅取决于确认谁已完成登记，也取决于核实与每项登记相关的信息是否准确且一致。他说：“选民登记册的可信度不仅取决于谁已完成登记，还取决于与每项登记相关的信息是否准确、一致且可核验。”Adegbuyi的提议将地理信息与身份信息和生物特征数据并列，纳入加强尼日利亚选举基础设施的更广泛框架。这一方法除其他作用外，还将为选举管理人员提供额外工具，用于分析选民位置分布模式，并找出需要进一步审查的记录。他说，当前围绕选民登记册的担忧，为重新审视能够提高核验和问责水平的技术方法提供了机会，以便在未来选举前加以改进。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕Creek Road 35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区以及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台报道政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛中产阶层的话题，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化和技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信任事业，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育、社区，以及人与社会的交叉议题。您可以发送电子邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.summary_zh: （首爾=聯合新聞社）記者申昌永=中國正快速擴大其市場版圖，不僅限於消費品和中間產品，在工業設備市場的布局也在加速。有觀點指出，韓國若要應對這一趨勢，就必須在先進市場突出供應可靠性，並在新兴市場鎖定生產工藝升級的需求。韓國貿易協會國際貿易通商研究員在1日發布的《中國工業設備出口的崛起與全球供應結構變化》報告中作出上述表述。
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.body: (서울=연합뉴스) 신창용 기자 = 중국이 소비재와 중간재를 넘어 산업설비 시장에서도 영역을 빠르게 넓히고 있는 것으로 나타났다. 한국이 이에 대응하려면 선진 시장에서는 공급 신뢰성을 내세우고 신흥 시장에서는 생산공정 고도화 수요를 공략해야 한다는 지적이 나왔다. 한국무역협회 국제무역통상연구원은 1일 발표한 '중국 산업설비 수출의 부상과 글로벌 공급구조 변화' 보고서에서 이같이 밝혔다. 보고서에 따르면 중국의 산업설비 수출액은 2015년 1천42억달러에서 2025년 2천572억달러로 약 2.5배 급증했다. 이는 연평균 8.2% 증가한 수준으로, 같은 기간 소비재(1.8%)와 중간재(6.0%)의 성장세를 크게 웃도는 수치다. 중국의 역할이 소비재·중간재 공급자를 넘어 글로벌 제조업 생산 기반을 제공하는 설비 공급자로 확장되고 있는 셈이다. 한국과 중국의 산업설비 수출경합도(ESI)는 2015년 46에서 2025년 54로 상승했다. 독일(55→62)과 일본(44→47)도 중국과의 경합도가 동반 상승했다. 중국은 기존에 강점을 보였던 전력설비와 식품·섬유가공기계 외에도 물류·이송설비에서 독일을 제쳤다. 범용·기타 설비 부문에서는 독일과 공동 1위로 올라서는 등 범용성 높은 분야를 중심으로 글로벌 공급 영향력을 크게 넓혔다. 중국의 산업설비 점유율은 신흥 시장에서 2015년 21.1%에서 2024년 29.6%로 급등했으나 미국의 통상 제재 영향이 미친 선진 시장에서는 12.8%에서 14.0%로 소폭 상승하는 데 그쳤다. 보고서는 독일과 일본의 점유율이 동반 하락하는 사이 한국이 3.0%에서 3.3%로 안정적인 입지를 유지한 선진 시장에서는 공급 신뢰성과 현지 대응 역량을 바탕으로 입지를 넓힐 수 있다고 평가했다. 반면 중국의 저가 공세로 한국 점유율이 6.3%에서 4.1%로 하락한 신흥 시장에서는 생산기지 신규·증설 초기 단계부터 참여해 설비 조달 기회를 선점하고, 이후 자동화와 고정밀화, 설비 교체 수요까지 연계해야 한다고 제언했다. 허슬비 무역협회 연구원은 "중국이 가격경쟁력을 앞세워 산업설비 공급을 빠르게 늘리고 있는 만큼 우리 기업은 품질과 납기 신뢰성, 부품 공급·유지보수 역량으로 차별화해야 한다"며 "정부 차원에서도 현지 인증 대응과 수요기업 발굴 지원 등을 강화해 우리 기업의 해외 진출 부담을 낮춰야 한다"고 강조했다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/11/01 11:29 송고 2026년11월01일 11시29분 송고
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.title_zh: 中国工业设备出口激增……“韩国应以质量、交付和售后服务应对”
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.body_zh:
（首尔=韩联社）记者申창용报道称，中国正在消费产品和中间产品之外，迅速扩大在工业设备市场的影响范围。有观点指出，韩国若要加以应对，就必须在发达市场突出供应可靠性，并在新兴市场开拓生产流程升级需求。韩国贸易协会国际贸易研究员1日发布的《中国工业设备出口的跃升与全球供应结构变化》报告称，工业设备出口额从2015年的1042亿美元增至2025年的2572亿美元，约为原来的2.5倍，年均增长率达到8.2%，远高于同期消费产品（1.8%）和中间产品（6.0%）的增长速度。这意味着，中国正从消费产品和中间产品供应国，扩展为为全球制造业生产基础提供设备的供应国。
韩国与中国工业设备出口竞争度（ESI）从2015年的46升至2025年的54。德国（55→62）和日本（44→47）与中国之间的竞争度也同步上升。除电力设备以及食品、纺织加工机械等原有优势领域外，中国在物流和输送设备方面也超过德国。在通用及其他设备领域，中国升至与德国并列第一，广泛扩大了在全球供应领域的影响力。
报告称，中国工业设备市场占有率在新兴市场从2015年的21.1%大幅升至2024年的29.6%；但在受美国贸易制裁影响的发达市场，仅从12.8%小幅升至14.0%。报告评价称，在德国和日本市场占有率同步下降的情况下，韩国在发达市场通过将占有率稳定在3.0%至3.3%，可以凭借供应可靠性和当地应对能力扩大市场影响力。
报告建议，在因中国低价攻势而使韩国市场占有率从6.3%降至4.1%的新兴市场，韩国企业应从生产基地新建和扩建初期就参与其中，先行获取设备采购机会，之后再将自动化、高精度化以及设备更新需求一并开发。
韩国贸易协会研究员具晓日（허슬비）强调：“中国凭借价格竞争力迅速扩大工业设备供应，因此我国企业应通过质量、交货期可靠性以及零部件供应和维护能力实现差异化。政府层面也应加强当地认证应对措施，并支持挖掘需求企业，以减轻我国企业出海面临的负担。”

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the appointment of Professor Murtala Muhammad Ahmad as the seventh substantive Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH), Sokoto. In a statement by the Head, Public Affairs, UDUTH, Mansur Wadata, the appointment is for an initial term of four years with effect from October 20, 2026, and was conveyed in a letter signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Professor Ahmad succeeds Professor Anas Ahmad Sabir, who successfully completed his two-term tenure in May this year. The statement further stated that while congratulating him on the appointment, Professor Pate reminded him of the heavy responsibilities of his new office and the yearnings of Nigerians for an effective and responsive healthcare delivery system. He urged the new CMD to justify the confidence reposed in him by Mr. President by working collaboratively with all stakeholders to ensure that the hospital continues to deliver quality healthcare services to Nigerians. Professor Ahmad becomes the second alumnus of the Usmanu Danfodiyo University to lead the Teaching Hospital as Chief Medical Director, marking a historic milestone for the institution. With over two decades of experience in Paediatrics and Child Health, Professor Ahmad brings a robust blend of clinical expertise, university teaching, and hospital administration to his new role. He earned his Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree from the Usmanu Danfodiyo University, followed by a Fellowship of the West African College of Physicians (FWACP) in Paediatrics and a Professional Diploma in Education from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. He also holds specialized certifications in paediatric electroencephalography, health leadership, management, and public administration from the University of Cape Town, University of Washington and Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) respectively. Before his elevation, Professor Ahmad built an impressive administrative track record within both the university and the teaching hospital, steadily climbing the academic ladder from Lecturer I to Senior Lecturer, Reader, and ultimately Professor of Paediatrics. He previously served as Deputy Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee (Training) at UDUTH for four years, where he brought impactful transformation to the administration of residency and training in the hospital. He also held key roles as Deputy Director of the Institute of Child Health and Faculty Examinations Officer in the Faculty of Clinical Sciences, alongside representing the faculty on the University Senate, and stepped in as Acting Chairman of the Medical Advisory Committee and Acting Chief Medical Director on multiple occasions. Beyond institutional management, Professor Ahmad has been at the forefront of public health service and specialised medical research in Sokoto State and across Nigeria, with active involvement in maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response, and as a national trainer on the management of severe acute malnutrition. As a prolific researcher, he has published widely in peer-reviewed journals focusing on child health, child neurology, epilepsy, and broader paediatric health concerns, while actively mentoring the next generation of medical professionals and postgraduate students. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.title_zh: Tinubu任命Ahmad教授为UDUTH首席医疗官
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/31/t.body_zh: 总统Bola Ahmed Tinubu已批准任命Murtala Muhammad Ahmad教授为位于Sokoto的Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital（UDUTH）第七任正式首席医务主任（CMD）。UDUTH公共事务负责人Mansur Wadata在一份声明中表示，此次任命的首个任期为4年，自2026年10月20日起生效，任命通知由卫生与社会保障协调部长Muhammad Ali Pate教授签署的函件传达。Pate教授在声明中进一步表示，他祝贺Ahmad教授获得任命，同时提醒他将承担新职位赋予的重任，以及尼日利亚人民对高效且能及时回应的医疗服务体系的期待。他敦促新任CMD通过与所有利益相关方协作，不辜负总统先生对他的信任，确保医院继续为尼日利亚人民提供优质医疗服务。Ahmad教授成为第二位以首席医务主任身份领导该教学医院的Usmanu Danfodiyo University校友，标志该校迎来历史性里程碑。Ahmad教授拥有20多年的儿科和儿童健康经验，将丰富的临床专业能力、大学教学经验和医院管理经验融入新职位。他从Usmanu Danfodiyo University取得医学学士与外科学士（MBBS）学位，随后取得西非内科医师学院（FWACP）儿科专业进修资格，并从Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria取得教育专业文凭。他还从University of Cape Town取得儿科脑电图和健康领导力认证，从University of Washington取得管理认证，并从Administrative Staff College of Nigeria（ASCON）取得公共行政认证。在此次晋升之前，Ahmad教授在大学和教学医院都取得了出色的行政管理成绩，并逐步晋升学术职级，先后担任一级讲师、高级讲师、Reader，最终成为儿科教授。他此前在UDUTH担任医学咨询委员会（培训）副主席4年，期间推动医院住院医师培训及培训管理工作的 impactful 转型。他还曾担任儿童健康研究所副所长、临床科学学院考试事务官等重要职务，代表学院参加大学评议会，并多次代理医学咨询委员会主席和首席医务主任职务。除机构管理外，Ahmad教授还一直处于Sokoto州及尼日利亚各地公共卫生服务和专业医疗研究的前沿，积极参与孕产妇和围产期死亡监测与应对工作，并担任重度急性营养不良管理领域的全国培训师。作为成果丰硕的研究者，他在同行评审期刊上广泛发表研究论文，重点关注儿童健康、儿童神经病学、癫痫以及更广泛的儿科健康问题，同时积极指导下一代医疗专业人员和研究生。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria，并在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。该报是面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛中产阶层的尼日利亚最具权威性的全平台新闻媒体，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供汇聚新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报秉持公共信托精神，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围从突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区延伸至人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送电子邮件至hello@thisdaylive.com或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body: R ecent reports confirming the killing of 80 people in bandits’ attacks on the Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State have continued to break hearts, raising concerns about the federal government’s weakening capacity to protect the lives of Nigerians. The report recorded that the attack, which led to massive looting of shops and market stalls and setting of houses ablaze, occurred on Friday, October 23, the community’s weekly market day. The incident to place on a day when traders and buyers from surrounding settlements converged to exchange farm produce, food and other goods, just shortly after Juma’at prayers. Residents said the assailants stormed the community on motorcycles from neighbouring Plateau State, and carried out the four-hour reign of terror unchallenged. By the time the attackers withdrew, residents were searching nearby bushes and a river for their missing relatives, while burnt houses, damaged shops and abandoned belongings testified to the scale of the destruction. On the day of the deadly attack, the Taraba State Police Command said only 10 bodies were recovered, but the next day, it said the death toll had risen to 58, including 15 people who drowned while fleeing in an overloaded canoe. The police spokesperson, Victor Mshelizah, said search operations led to the recovery of additional bodies from surrounding bushes. By Tuesday, it was gathered that the death toll had further risen to 80. Beyond the loss of lives and property, the attack has renewed concerns about the ability of security agencies to protect isolated and vulnerable communities across the country. A trader identified only as Adamu said the assailants operated for hours without resistance. “We have no government in place,” he said, describing the duration of the attack and the destruction of goods during the market raid. Following the attack, the police announced the deployment of additional personnel, alongside the Nigerian Army and other security agencies. Residents were urged to remain calm, stay vigilant and provide credible information to security operatives. Condemning the killing, the global human rights organisation, Amnesty International, accused the federal government of failing to adequately protect vulnerable rural communities from repeated deadly attacks by gunmen and terrorists. The human rights organisation, in a statement, said the attack demonstrated a “disdain for the sanctity of life” and called for an impartial investigation, justice for the victims and adequate reparations for survivors. It said the incident reflected a wider pattern of violence against rural communities in parts of northern Nigeria, where armed groups have repeatedly attacked settlements, killed residents, destroyed property and abducted people. It further criticised the Nigerian authorities for what it described as their failure to prevent recurring atrocities and ensure that suspected perpetrators were brought to justice. The latest attack occurred despite Governor Agbu Kefas’ earlier intervention. Last January, he declared Karim-Lamido a special area of security concern through Executive Order No. 1 of 2026, citing recurring communal clashes, bandit-related attacks and violent herders’ attackers. The declaration was aimed at strengthening efforts to restore peace, protect residents and create conditions for normal economic and social activities. But violence has continued to threaten communities in the area. Observers feel that the Binnari killings are part of a wider pattern of insecurity in Taraba, where communal clashes, banditry, kidnapping and attacks on rural settlements have repeatedly threatened lives and livelihoods. The entire local government has featured prominently in the violence. Its location near the boundaries with Plateau, Bauchi and Gombe states added a cross-border dimension to security operations, particularly where armed groups can move through rural settlements and difficult terrain. In general, banditry has become a growing problem in North-west and North-central, with powerful gangs battling overstretched police and military across hard-to-reach, rural locations. Driven by money rather than ideology, the bandits in Nigeria target poorly policed rural areas, kidnapping for ransom and killing residents. The terror gangs raid villages and impose “taxes” on farmers and mining operations in areas with little state presence. The Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED), an independent, non-profit global research organisation and conflict monitor, recorded thousands of deaths (over 13,485 killed across North-Western states between 2010 and 2023, with a sharp surge of 2,742 casualties across 599 incidents in 2025 alone). Hundreds of thousands have been displaced. Bandits operate not as a single army, but as a loose “franchise” of over 120 armed groups led by regional commanders known as kachalas. Their tactics include mass motorcycle-borne raids, village destruction and looting, kidnap-for-ransom operations, cattle rustling, and imposing illegal “protection taxes” on farmers and miners. Originating from historical attacks on farmers and destruction of farmlands by herders, the crisis expanded due to climate change, shrinking grazing lands, poverty, gold-funded arms smuggling, and vast, unpoliced forested sanctuaries. The Nigerian military regularly launches air strikes and ground sweeps, yet they seem to be growing by the day. Local and state governments have occasionally attempted localised amnesties or peace talks, which critics and defence analysts argue fail because the gangs lack political ideology and repeatedly break truces. The primary responsibility of any government is securing the lives and property of its citizens, but the people hardly see this being demonstrated each time. As sad as the deaths were, there was not a single reaction or statement from the President Bola Tinubu and the Presidency, even as a succour to the community. Even though President Tinubu has repeatedly ordered troops to pursue suspected terrorists responsible for these mass killings of people across the country, Nigerians are yet to see any significant improvement, as people are still being killed almost daily. It was only the Senate that called for an urgent security offensive in border communities across Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states. The lawmakers urged security agencies to establish additional security camps and intensify surveillance in the affected areas to prevent further attacks and protect vulnerable communities. The upper legislative chamber noted that the continued activities of armed bandits in rural communities undermined the government’s constitutional responsibility to protect lives and property. It warned that failure to address the recurring attacks could lead to further loss of lives, destruction of property, displacement of residents and worsening humanitarian challenges, and that no community should be left at the mercy of armed criminal groups. There is no country where the leaders truly value human lives that will not be jolted by the loss of 80 lives. In normal climes, the attack is enough to declare a state of emergency on insecurity in the state until the perpetrators are fished out and dealt with appropriately. But in Nigeria where the authorities and citizens are inundated with frequent news of massive killing, nothing bothers them anymore. Until authorities demonstrate that vulnerable communities such as Binnari are adequately protected, the killings will remain a grim reminder of the gap between official security commitments and the safety residents experience on the ground. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.title_zh: 塔拉巴州杀人案频发与治理危机
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body_zh: 最新报道证实，武装劫匪袭击塔拉巴州卡里姆拉米多地方政府辖区宾纳里社区，造成80人死亡，消息不断令人痛心，也引发人们对联邦政府保护尼日利亚人生命安全能力削弱的担忧。报道称，袭击发生于10月23日星期五，即该社区每周一次的集市日。袭击导致大量商店和市场摊位遭洗劫，房屋被纵火焚毁。当天，附近聚居地的商贩和买家聚集在社区内 exchanged 农产品、食品及其他商品，事件就发生在他们刚刚结束主麻聚礼不久之后。居民称，袭击者从邻近的 Plateau 州骑摩托车冲入社区，并在无人抵抗的情况下持续了4小时的恐怖统治。袭击者撤离时，居民正在附近的灌木丛和河中寻找失踪的亲人，被焚毁的房屋、受损的商店和被遗弃的物品则见证了破坏的严重程度。致命袭击当天，塔拉巴州警察司令部表示仅发现10具遗体；但第二天又称，死亡人数已升至58人，其中包括15人在乘坐超载独木舟逃离时溺亡。警方发言人 Victor Mshelizah 表示，搜索行动从周边灌木丛中发现了更多遗体。到星期二，人们获悉死亡人数进一步升至80人。除了生命和财产损失外，此次袭击再次引发人们对安全机构保护全国偏远、脆弱社区能力的担忧。一名仅透露姓名为 Adamu 的商贩说，袭击者长达数小时未遇抵抗。他描述了袭击持续时间以及市场突袭中货物遭破坏的情况，并说：“我们这里没有政府。”袭击发生后，警方宣布增派人员，同时由尼日利亚陆军及其他安全机构配合行动。居民被敦促保持冷静、提高警惕，并向安全人员提供可靠信息。全球人权组织大赦国际谴责此次杀戮，指责联邦政府未能充分保护脆弱农村社区，使其免遭持枪犯罪分子和恐怖分子反复发动的致命袭击。该人权组织在一份声明中表示，此次袭击显示出对“生命神圣性”的蔑视，并呼吁开展公正调查，为受害者伸张正义，并给予幸存者充分赔偿。该组织称，这起事件反映了尼日利亚北部部分地区针对农村社区的更广泛暴力模式；武装团体一再袭击聚居地、杀害居民、破坏财产并绑架人口。该组织还批评尼日利亚当局未能阻止暴行再次发生，也未能确保将疑似犯罪者绳之以法。尽管州长 Agbu Kefas 此前采取了干预措施，最新袭击仍然发生。今年1月，他通过2026年第1号行政命令，将卡里姆拉米多列为特别安全关注地区，理由是当地社区冲突不断发生、武装劫匪袭击频仍，以及暴力牧民袭击事件。该声明旨在加强恢复和平、保护居民以及为正常经济和社会活动创造条件的工作。然而，暴力活动仍在威胁该地区社区。观察人士认为，宾纳里惨案是塔拉巴州更广泛安全局势恶化的一部分；当地社区冲突、匪患、绑架和针对农村聚居地的袭击一再威胁生命和生计。整个地方政府辖区在暴力事件中首当其冲。该地靠近 Plateau、Bauchi 和 Gombe 三州边界，为安全行动增加了跨境因素，尤其是在武装团体能够经由农村聚居地和崎岖地形流动的情况下。总体而言，武装匪患已成为尼日利亚西北部和中北部日益严重的问题，强大的犯罪团伙在难以抵达的偏远农村与警力不足、兵力吃紧的警察和军队抗衡。这些劫匪受金钱而非意识形态驱动，袭击治安薄弱的农村地区，通过绑架勒索赎金并杀害居民牟利。恐怖团伙突袭村庄，在国家力量鲜少介入的地区向农民和采矿活动征收“税费”。武装冲突地点与事件数据项目（ACLED）是一家独立、非营利的全球研究组织和冲突监测机构。该机构记录了数千人死亡：2010年至2023年期间，西北部各州共有超过13,485人死亡；仅2025年，599起事件便造成2,742人伤亡，增幅显著。数十万人被迫流离失所。武装劫匪并非作为单一军队行动，而是由120多个武装团体构成的松散“加盟网络”，由被称为 kachalas 的地区指挥官领导。他们惯用的手段包括大规模摩托车突袭、摧毁村庄、洗劫财物、绑架勒索、盗掠牲畜，以及向农民和矿工征收非法“保护费”。这场危机起源于牧民对农民的历史性袭击和农地破坏，随后因气候变化、牧场萎缩、贫困、由黄金资金支持的武器走私，以及大片缺乏治安管理的森林避难所而扩大。尼日利亚军方经常发动空袭和地面清剿，但袭击似乎仍在与日俱增。地方政府和州政府偶尔会尝试局部特赦或和平谈判，但批评者和国防分析人士认为，这些努力无法奏效，因为这些团伙缺乏政治理念，并且屡次违背停火协议。任何政府的首要责任都是保障公民生命和财产安全，但民众几乎看不到这一点在每一次事件中得到体现。死亡人数令人悲痛，但总统 Bola Tinubu 和总统府对此次袭击没有作出任何反应或声明，也没有向社区提供任何慰问。尽管 Tinubu 总统已多次命令部队追捕涉嫌制造全国多地大规模杀戮的恐怖分子，尼日利亚人仍未看到局势有显著改善，几乎每天仍有人丧生。只有参议院呼吁在塔拉巴州、Plateau 州和 Bauchi 州的边境社区紧急开展安全攻势。议员敦促安全机构设立更多安全营地，并加强受影响地区的监视，以防止进一步袭击并保护脆弱社区。参议院指出，武装劫匪持续在 rural 社区活动，削弱了政府保护生命和财产的宪法责任。参议院警告，若不处理反复发生的袭击，可能造成更多人员死亡、财产破坏、居民流离失所和人道主义挑战加剧，任何社区都不应落入武装犯罪集团的魔掌。80条生命的丧失足以震动任何真正珍视人生命的国家。在正常情况下，此次袭击已足以促使该州就安全问题宣布紧急状态，直至抓获肇事者并依法处置。但在尼日利亚，当局和公民不断看到大规模杀戮的消息，已经不会再为此感到不安。在当局证明已对宾纳里等脆弱社区提供充分保护之前，这些杀戮仍将是官方安全承诺与居民实际安全之间巨大落差的冷酷提醒。THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.summary: Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, sparked widespread outrage recently after issuing a stern warning that anyone caught manipulating the 2027 elections would be killed. Speaking at a political event in his constituency, Omo-Agege warned that anyone who attempted to rig or manipulate votes in the upcoming polls would face severe consequences. Omo-Agege’s comment was not only unfortunate but unguarded and totally condemnable.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.summary_zh: 前參議院副議長歐維·歐莫-阿格吉參議員近日因嚴厲警告任何被抓到操縱2027年選舉的人都將被殺，引發廣泛憤怒。歐莫-阿格吉在其選區的一場政治活動上警告，任何企圖在即將舉行的投票中舞弊或操縱選票的人都將面臨嚴重後果。歐莫-阿格吉的言論不僅令人遗憾，而且缺乏謹慎，完全應受譴責。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.body: Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, sparked widespread outrage recently after issuing a stern warning that anyone caught manipulating the 2027 elections would be killed. Speaking at a political event in his constituency, Omo-Agege warned that anyone who attempted to rig or manipulate votes in the upcoming polls would face severe consequences. Addressing supporters and party faithful in Delta Central, Omo-Agege declared that the era of political actors subverting the popular mandate was over. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central senatorial seat under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), emphasised that voters were prepared to defend their votes at polling units nationwide. “I want to make the news again. Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him! If you don’t value your life, come and rig the election. They’re rigging your future. They’re rigging the future of your children. We’re waiting for them. Let them try it. It is rig-and- die. We’re going to give them aura for aura. There’s no court this time. We’re going to fight,” he was quoted as saying. Omo-Agege declared his intention to contest for the Delta Central senatorial seat in the 2027 elections in May. He resigned his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in a letter dated May and addressed to the chairman of the party’s Orogun Ward 2 in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Omo-Agege’s comment was not only unfortunate but unguarded and totally condemnable. He should know that it is inappropriate for a man of his calibre to advocate for jungle justice. As a lawyer and a former lawmaker, he should know that the best way to treat anybody arrested for a crime, is to be handed over to the police for prosecution. The police should invite him for questioning, and if possible, to write an undertaking that he will not encourage the killing of anyone during the 2027 general election. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/o.body_zh: 参议院前副议长、参议员奥维·奥莫-阿格吉近日因严厉警告称，任何操纵2027年选举的人都会被杀，引发广泛愤慨。奥莫-阿格吉在其选区的一场政治活动上警告称，任何企图在即将举行的选举中舞弊或操纵选票的人都将面临严重后果。他在向中三角洲州的支持者和党内人士发表讲话时宣称，政治人物颠覆民意的时代已经结束。奥莫-阿格吉正以尼日利亚民主党（NDC）候选人身份角逐中三角洲州联邦参议院席位，他强调，选民已准备好在全国各地的投票站捍卫自己的选票。据报道，他说：“我要再次成为新闻人物。任何人在那一天操纵选举，我们就会杀了他！如果你不珍惜自己的生命，就来操纵选举吧。他们正在操纵你的未来，操纵你孩子的未来。我们正等着他们。让他们试试看。那就是舞弊和死亡。我们将以同样的手段回敬他们。这次没有法庭。我们将抗争到底。”奥莫-阿格吉于5月宣布 intends 参加2027年中三角洲州联邦参议院席位选举。他在5月写给尼日利亚三角洲州乌盖利北地方政府辖区该党奥罗贡第2选区主席的一封信中，辞去了全尼日利亚进步大会党（APC）的党籍。奥莫-阿格吉的言论不仅不幸，而且缺乏审慎，完全应受谴责。他应当知道，像他这样资历的人鼓吹丛林司法并不合适。作为一名律师和前立法者，他理应懂得，对任何因犯罪被捕的人，最恰当的处理方式是将其移交警方起诉。警方应邀请他接受询问，并尽可能要求他签署承诺书，保证在2027年大选期间不鼓励杀害任何人。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层提供服务，同时充当抱负者和千禧一代探索新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。该报是一项公共信托，致力于追求真理与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区等议题，直面个人与社会之间的 crossroads。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/v.title: Votes are Near, Debts Keep Rising
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/v.summary: For citizens awaiting functioning hospitals, decent classrooms and reliable electricity, the concern is whether yesterday’s debts will consume tomorrow’s opportunities. Critics demand evidence that rising obligations are delivering benefits commensurate with their costs.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/v.summary_zh: 对于期待医院恢复正常运转、教室条件得到改善以及电力供应可靠的民众而言，他们担心的是昨天的债务是否会吞噬明天的机会。批评者要求拿出证据，证明不断上升的债务负担带来了与成本相称的收益。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/v.body: Nigeria’s next President will inherit two competing demands: the promises that win an election and the repayment schedules that survive it. For citizens awaiting functioning hospitals, decent classrooms and reliable electricity, the concern is whether yesterday’s debts will consume tomorrow’s opportunities. President Bola Tinubu’s latest defence of foreign borrowing sharpens that tension. His administration argues that loans will finance productive infrastructure, create jobs and support a $1 trillion economy by 2030. Critics demand evidence that rising obligations are delivering benefits commensurate with their costs. The immediate controversy concerns the request submitted to the Senate on October 27 for approximately $20.52 billion and €1.05 billion under the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. The proposed financing covers infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education and other programmes. With the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027, its implications extend beyond the administration seeking approval. In his essay, “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” circulated by presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu argues that borrowing should be assessed against the assets and opportunities it creates. His defence identifies the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity upgrades and port modernisation as investments intended to strengthen productive capacity. The administration also says it is pursuing longer financing tenors aligned with infrastructure lifespans. That is a substantive response to the criticism. Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit imposes costs on manufacturers, farmers and households. Roads that shorten journeys, ports that clear goods efficiently and electricity systems that reduce generator dependence can expand production and strengthen government revenue. However, an economically desirable project is not automatically an affordable financing proposition. Its value depends on construction costs, borrowing terms, completion time, maintenance and actual use. The President projects that the coastal highway could reduce logistics costs along its corridor by 15–20 per cent, support trade and tourism, and generate substantial direct and indirect employment. These remain anticipated benefits rather than established outcomes. Their eventual scale will depend on delivery and connections to farms, factories, ports and markets. A completed road may stimulate commerce; an unfinished corridor can accumulate financing costs while businesses continue bearing existing transport expenses. The distinction also applies to the $1 trillion economy ambition. Borrowed money can help create productive assets, but securing financing does not establish that the resulting investment will generate sufficient economic or fiscal returns. Tinubu’s response therefore places project execution at the centre of the debate. It also creates a measurable standard against which the administration’s borrowing decisions can be assessed. Existing obligations explain public unease. Debt Management Office figures put Nigeria’s total public debt at N166.79 trillion in June 2026, against N159.35 trillion in March. Domestic obligations accounted for N91.59 trillion and external debt for N75.20 trillion. The total includes federal, state and Federal Capital Territory liabilities. These figures require careful interpretation. Exchange-rate movements can change the naira value of foreign obligations without equivalent fresh borrowing. Legislative approval also differs from disbursement: facilities may be drawn gradually over several years. The more immediate constraint is revenue. The International Monetary Fund’s June assessment estimated federal interest payments at 53.2 per cent of federal revenue in 2025 and projected 53.7 per cent for 2026. These figures cover interest, not total debt service including principal repayments. This pressure limits resources for competing priorities. A government can continue paying creditors while delaying contractors, squeezing public services or postponing capital projects. In his commentary, “Borrowing Is Not a Good Governance”, Ibrahim Muhammad Sani expresses the frustration underlying the controversy: government should demonstrate repaired schools, functioning healthcare centres, paid pensions and accountable expenditure. His strongest challenge is straightforward. What did earlier borrowing deliver? Tinubu’s response acknowledges the importance of tangible results. But the administration must connect financing announcements to identifiable projects, expenditure records and completed assets. The IMF’s assessment offers a similarly qualified picture: reforms have improved macroeconomic outcomes and resilience, while conditions remain difficult for many Nigerians. Aggregate improvement and household hardship can coexist. For families struggling with food, transport and energy costs, projected infrastructure gains will become persuasive when they translate into jobs, lower expenses and better services. The proposed shift towards longer financing tenors deserves scrutiny. Matching repayment periods to asset lifespans can reduce refinancing pressure, but longer maturity alone does not establish affordability. Lawmakers need each facility’s interest rate, fees, currency, grace period, maturity and repayment schedule. They also need project appraisals, procurement arrangements, implementation milestones and evidence of readiness. Foreign-currency loans introduce another exposure. Where revenues accrue mainly in naira, depreciation can increase the domestic cost of servicing dollar and euro obligations. Infrastructure may generate broad economic benefits without directly earning foreign exchange. Scrutiny should therefore establish how repayments will be funded under less favourable revenue and exchange-rate conditions. Publishing the performance of previously financed projects would strengthen that assessment. A second Tinubu administration would meet these obligations alongside renewed campaign promises. An opposition government would inherit the same contracts while seeking resources for its own programme. However, without facility-level repayment schedules, it would be misleading to suggest that all the proposed borrowing must be repaid during the next presidential term. The administration has presented an economic case for borrowing. Its credibility rests on sustainable terms, transparent expenditure and completed projects. Nigerians will choose their next government at the polls. The financing decisions taken now will help determine how much that government can deliver. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/v.title_zh: 投票日临近，债务继续攀升
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/v.body_zh:
尼日利亚下一任总统将继承两种相互竞争的要求：赢得选举所需的承诺，以及选举后仍能承受的还款安排。对于期待医院恢复正常运转、拥有合格教室和可靠电力的公民而言，他们担心的是昨日的债务是否会吞噬明天的机会。总统博拉· Tinubu最近为对外借款所作的辩护加剧了这种紧张局势。他的政府主张，贷款将用于建设生产性基础设施、创造就业，并支持尼日利亚在2030年前实现1万亿美元经济体量。批评者要求拿出证据，证明不断上升的债务负担所带来的收益与其成本相称。

当前争议涉及政府于10月27日向参议院提交的一项申请：根据2026—2027年补充外部借款计划，寻求约205.2亿美元和10.5亿欧元融资。拟议融资将用于基础设施、农业、医疗保健、教育及其他项目。总统选举定于2027年1月16日举行，因此此事的影响超出了寻求批准的政府本身。

总统发言人Bayo Onanuga散发的文章《从改革到交付：我们的基础设施投资与增长战略》中，Tinubu主张，应根据借款创造的资产和机会来评估借款。他的辩护将拉各斯—卡巴莱海岸公路、索科托—巴达吉里超级公路、跨撒哈拉超级公路、电力升级和港口现代化列为旨在增强生产能力的投资。政府还表示，正在争取与基础设施使用寿命相匹配的更长期融资期限。

这是对批评意见的实质性回应。尼日利亚的基础设施缺口给制造商、农民和家庭带来成本。缩短行程的道路、高效疏运货物的港口以及减少对发电机依赖的电力系统，能够扩大生产并增加政府收入。然而，经济上理想的项目并不会自动成为融资上可负担的方案。其价值取决于建设成本、借款条件、完工时间、维护费用和实际使用情况。

总统预计，海岸公路可使其沿线物流成本降低15%—20%，促进贸易和旅游业，并创造大量直接和间接就业。这些仍是预期收益，而非已经实现的结果。其最终规模将取决于项目交付情况，以及能否连接农场、工厂、港口和市场。一条完工的道路可能刺激商业往来；一条未完工的交通走廊则可能在企业继续承担现有运输费用的同时，不断累积融资成本。这种区别同样适用于实现1万亿美元经济体的目标。借入资金可以帮助创造生产性资产，但获得融资并不等于相关投资必然产生足够的经济或财政回报。

因此，Tinubu的回应把项目执行置于争论中心，也确立了一项可衡量的标准，以便据此评估政府的借款决策。现有债务负担解释了公众的不安。债务管理办公室的数据显示，尼日利亚公共债务总额从2026年3月的159.35万亿奈拉上升至同年6月的166.79万亿奈拉。其中，国内债务为91.59万亿奈拉，外债为75.20万亿奈拉。总额包括联邦、州及联邦首都区的债务。这些数字需要谨慎解读。汇率波动可以在没有新增借款的情况下改变外债的奈拉计价价值。立法批准也不等同于资金拨付：相关融资额度可能在数年内逐步提取。当下更直接的约束是财政收入。国际货币基金组织6月份的评估估计，2025年联邦利息支出占联邦收入的53.2%，并预计2026年这一比例为53.7%。这些数字仅涵盖利息，不包括本金偿还在内的全部债务偿付。这种压力限制了政府满足其他竞争性优先事项的资源。政府可以继续向债权人付款，同时拖延承包商、挤压公共服务或推迟资本项目。

在评论文章《借款并非良好治理》中，Ibrahim Muhammad Sani表达了争议背后的不满：政府应当展示修缮后的学校、正常运转的医疗中心、已发放的养老金以及问责明确的支出。他提出的最有力质疑十分直接：此前借入的资金带来了什么？Tinubu的回应承认了 tangible results的重要性，但政府必须把融资公告与明确的项目、支出记录和完工资产对应起来。

国际货币基金组织的评估同样给出了一幅带有保留的图景：改革改善了宏观经济表现和韧性，但许多尼日利亚人的处境仍然困难。总体改善与家庭困境可以并存。对于在食品、交通和能源成本方面苦苦挣扎的家庭而言，只有当预期中的基础设施收益转化为就业、开支下降和更好的服务时，这些收益才会真正具有说服力。

转向更长期融资期限值得审查。让还款期与资产使用寿命相匹配，可以减轻再融资压力，但仅有更长的到期期限并不能证明融资方案可负担。议员需要了解每项融资的利率、费用、货币、宽限期、期限和还款安排，还需要项目评估、采购安排、实施里程碑以及准备就绪的证据。外币贷款还带来另一种风险敞口。如果政府收入主要以奈拉取得，奈拉贬值可能增加偿付美元和欧元债务的国内成本。基础设施可以产生广泛的经济效益，却未必直接赚取外汇。因此，审查应确认在收入和汇率条件不利时，偿还资金将如何筹措。公布此前受融资支持项目的绩效，将有助于加强这种评估。

Tinubu的第二届政府将在承担这些债务的同时，再次作出竞选承诺。反对党政府也会继承同样的合同，并寻求资源来实施自己的方案。然而，在没有逐项融资还款安排的情况下，暗示所有拟议借款都必须在下一届总统任期内偿还，会造成误导。

政府已经为借款提出了经济理由，其可信度取决于融资条件是否可持续、支出是否透明以及项目是否完工。尼日利亚人将在投票站选择下一届政府。当前作出的融资决策，将有助于决定这届政府能够交付多少成果。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/b.body: righton gained quick revenge after being knocked out of the Carabao Cup in midweek by stunning Manchester City and condemning Enzo Maresca’s side to back-to-back Premier League defeats. Fabian Hurzeler’s men had twice taken the lead at Etihad Stadium on Wednesday but were edged out on penalties. On Saturday, they held on to a highly impressive victory to move just two points behind City in third. Brighton scored the winning goal just 11 minutes in courtesy of a major helping hand from right-back Matheus Nunes, whose miscued clearance fell nicely for Yasin Ayari to convert from close range. City should have levelled 10 minutes later when Iliman Ndiaye rose to meet Elliot Anderson’s cross but planted his header the wrong side of the post, before the Senegal international stung Bart Verbruggen’s palms at the near post. Ndiaye was proving to be City’s brightest spark as they looked for a way back into the game in the second half and the ex-Everton man ran clear and thumped a strike which was brilliantly tipped onto the crossbar by Verbruggen. The Brighton goalkeeper was proving to be a difficult prospect to find a way past and he made another superb save to deny Nunes, while a weak header from Erling Haaland was more comfortable to deal with. City’s star striker Haaland was being starved of any real service and his side could well have fallen further behind at the other end – Maxim de Cuyper blazing over from 10 yards out and then forcing Donnarumma into a sharp save with a header. But those missed opportunities from Brighton did not matter as they collected all three points to continue their exciting start to the season. Meanwhile, Taiwo Awoniyi opened his goal account for the season yesterday. Awoniyi, who recently returned from suspension, scored at the end of the first half to help Coventry City secure a 3-1 victory over Sunderland. The Nigeria international showed good determination to win possession from Sunderland defender Luke O’Nien before driving into the box and firing past goalkeeper Robin Roefs. Awoniyi’s strike marked his first goal for the Sky Blues in the Premier League and his second in eight appearances across all competitions since joining from Nottingham Forest in the summer. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.title: The Leadership Nigeria Badly Needs
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.summary: So many things trouble me about the quality of leadership in Nigeria, and this did not help matters. It further exposes the character of leadership in Nigeria. There is something about leadership in Nigeria that displays a lack of focus and empathy.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.summary_zh: 尼日利亚领导层的质量有太多令人担忧之处，而这起事件无疑让情况更加恶化。它进一步暴露了尼日利亚领导层的某些特征。尼日利亚的领导层存在一种缺失专注与同理心的表现。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body: SIMONKOLAWOLELIVE! simon.kolawole@thisdaylive.com, sms: 0805 500 1961 Let’s just say I have not been in the best of spirits for a while. Many things about our dearly beloved country have been weighing on my mind. This was compounded on Monday evening at the photography exhibition by ‘Fisayo Soyombo, whom I call “Nigeria’s No. 1 Daredevil Journalist”. He had gone undercover, posing as an aspiring migrant who desired to reach Italy via the Libya route. He spent 47 days on the road, from the take-off point in Kano, Nigeria, onward to Tripoli, Libya, where the traffickers usually dump their “clients”. He told the agonising story of dehumanisation, rape and death. He terminated his trip at Tripoli, having taken a trove of images that vividly tell the sad story. Soyombo made a number of profound points. One, the migrants themselves are victims. Many are melting under the economic heat in Nigeria. We cannot blame them for seeking greener pastures. They are promised heaven and earth by the traffickers. Even internally, many Nigerians daily leave their villages for Lagos and Abuja because of the promise of a better life. You can, therefore, hardly blame Nigerians for looking to Europe for a better life. Migration, if done properly, is not an iniquity. From creation, humans have always relocated from their homelands for economic reasons. The problem is not the desire to leave; it is the deadly, illegal route and the traffickers who profit from it. Two, Soyombo said would-be irregular migrants are not unaware of the dangers, but they always hope their own stories will be different. To them, staying back in Nigeria is not an option. Their resolve is akin to that of the four men with leprosy who sat outside the gates of Samaria after the city was besieged by Syrian soldiers, as told in the Bible. Facing certain death from starvation, they asked themselves, “Why should we sit here waiting to die? If we say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die.” They decided to surrender to the Syrians, saying: “If they kill us, then we die.” It was also similar to Esther’s “if I perish, I perish”. Really, it would be easy for me to sit here and castigate those running abroad by any means in search of pastures new, but I am not in their shoes. I am relatively comfortable. I am an employer. I can feed myself and my family. I can travel abroad for vacation. But there are millions of Nigerians living from hand to mouth. Their own realities are markedly different. They wake up every day hoping that life will be better, but many go to bed hungry and hopeless. They are very vulnerable to the promise of El Dorado and would do anything possible to get there. We may question the judgment of these irregular migrants, but we cannot minimise their despair and desperation. Who feels it knows it. After we had viewed 47 images from his 47-day clandestine voyage, Soyombo took questions from guests. He said since the publication of his three-part report on his experience, no government agency had got in touch with him, not even to seek his assistance with information that could help track the human traffickers. The take-off point was in Kano. There is a physical address. There are human agents and facilitators. There are bank account details involved. There are at least five government agencies whose responsibilities include tackling human trafficking, one way or another. Maybe they are investigating on their own, but what does it hurt to talk to a “participant-observer”? I went to bed feeling disheartened that a journalistic work of this significance did not get the needed attention of the authorities concerned. Apart from helping to track the traffickers, it would be potent material to warn those who are hell-bent on the trans-Saharan route to Europe. Soyombo revealed that many of those who embark on the journey end up with regrets. I instantly thought that this would be useful for enlightenment and orientation purposes. Could it be that the authorities are tired of chasing leads? Could it be that they did not see anything of value in Soyombo’s report? Or maybe they missed the report, although they all have public comms units that do media monitoring? So many things trouble me about the quality of leadership in Nigeria, and this did not help matters. I have been downcast over the reported circumstances surrounding the death of Mr Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, the gospel singer better known as Toluwanisings. He had a medical emergency but was rejected by “seven or eight hospitals”, according to his aide. In Nigeria, many emergency patients are callously denied life-saving care and die in dire circumstances. It happens all the time. Mind you, we have a law that forbids rejecting emergency patients, not to mention medical ethics and the spirit of the Hippocratic Oath. But this is what Nigeria has become. This is one reason many have lost hope. I have also been downcast about the power situation, which has been pathetic in many places, despite the outlandish claim by Mr Joseph Tegbe, minister of power, that some electricity consumers asked him to “slow down” with the “remarkable improvement in power supply” because items in their freezers were freezing. If that was meant to be a joke, it was in exceptionally bad taste. Utterly insensitive. Businesses are burning billions on petrol and diesel and this is a joke to a minister of the Federal Republic of Nigeria? I wouldn’t recommend kidding with something that is ruining the livelihoods of Nigerians. It further exposes the character of leadership in Nigeria. We can do better. There is something about leadership in Nigeria that displays a lack of focus and empathy. We are used to it. Look at the power situation again since 1999, when we transitioned to democracy. With serious leadership, the whole country could be enjoying uninterrupted power supply by now — even if we had started from zero, with no cables or transformers whatsoever. It is all about singleness of mind and tenacity of purpose. Nothing and no-one in this world can convince me that it is impossible to resolve the power crisis in 27 years. We can give all the excuses the world has to offer, but the bleeding truth is that we are just not a bunch of serious people. There is no nicer way of putting it. When you view everything together — the shocking situation of power supply, the inhospitable state of health care, the economic situation of the people in the same country where a jobless youth leader brazenly gives brand-new SUVs as gifts — you cannot but marvel at the level of leadership sensitivity in Nigeria. What does leadership actually mean to us? Seeing thousands of Nigerians leaving the country out of despondency and not doing much to give them hope? Seeing poor people being turned back at hospitals and forced to go home and die because “there is no bed space”? Seeing refuse heaps everywhere and flying to Dubai to celebrate the 60th birthday of a politician? Leadership is about responsiveness, but there is too much indifference in the land. Sometimes, I wonder how our leaders sleep at night in a society where health care centres do not function optimally, where emergency services hardly exist, where thousands of students are being taught chemistry without chemicals, and where many schools do not have libraries or laboratories. How can you be a council chair or a governor and not be touched by the sight of potholes and bad roads? How can you not be moved by the sight of communities without water? All these leadership failures are stripping ordinary citizens of hope and driving many of them into seeking trans-Saharan solutions. My conclusion has always been that we badly need a new kind of leadership — at every tier of government and in every agency. We need a new culture. We need a leadership culture that is focussed, responsible, sensitive and responsive. We discuss leadership issues all the time, but we often focus on competence. That is fundamental. But competence must come with compassion and concentration. We have to keep appealing to the collective consciences of our leaders at every opportunity. We have to keep reminding them of their responsibilities to the citizens. Making the lives of the people better must be the central focus of leadership, no matter who is in power. In truth, Nigerians are not asking for too much. All they want are leaders who truly care about them. The connection is just not there. The emotional gap between the leaders and the citizens is too wide. The president bears an enormous responsibility, but so do governors, council chairs, ministers and the heads of public agencies. Each must answer for the duties of their office. Our appeals to their consciences must be backed by a determination to hold them accountable. Nigerians deserve leaders who care enough to get things done. No Nigerian should feel so hopeless as to see the Sahara as the only way out. Giving people a reason to believe in their own country is the first duty of leadership. Mr Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the APC presidential campaign council, has claimed in an interview with ARISE that ministers paid billions of naira to secure appointments. I would be lying if I said I was hearing this allegation for the first time. I was still amazed, though, that this allegation was coming from a top member of the ruling party. Mr Felix Morka, the APC national publicity secretary, quickly moved to do some damage control. He said Hassan was talking about ministers in past administrations, not the ones serving under President Tinubu. Hmmm. Wouldn’t it be nice for ministers who served under Presidents Buhari, Jonathan and Obasanjo to speak up? Damning. The voter registration conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has run into a storm with the discovery of suspected AI-generated images. I am not a tech expert, so I may be limited in the comment I can make in this regard. But if a voter comes for physical capture, how could the image be AI-generated unless something funny is going on? I had thought some of those who registered online uploaded AI-generated images, but INEC said it had identified the officers behind it. INEC has a big job on its hands cleaning up the register. The commission usually displays the register for comments. It is now our duty to watch closely when the final register is made public. Vigilance. Does the opposition have a bigger campaign manager than “Professor” Taiwo Oyedele, the minister of finance? Almost every day, the tax expert provides campaign materials against President Tinubu for the opposition. He recently said fuel tax would be introduced “when the economy stabilises”, then tried to be too clever by half, tagging the reports “fake news” — yet the video he himself posted confirmed he said it. He has struck again, saying some households spend 120 percent of their income on food. He always puts his foot in his mouth but I had thought being a minister would help him. He sure enjoys the sound of his own voice. It is hard to save such people from themselves. Incurable. In what I consider a counter to Alhaji Atiku Abubakar’s economic hardship-focussed campaign strategy, the Tinubu administration has approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for civil servants for six months. But the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) has described the relief package as inadequate and instead demanded an immediate baseline salary increase to N300,000 for the lowest-paid workers. In fact, the union has rejected the N70,000 relief package. I was wondering why TUC would reject a bonus it did not negotiate for. In any case, if I were earning N70,000 and were offered an extra N70,000 as transport support, why should I reject it? Wonderful.

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/t.body_zh:
西蒙·科拉沃勒现场直播！simon.kolawole@thisdaylive.com，短信：0805 500 1961

先说一句吧，有一段时间以来，我的情绪一直不太好。我们深爱的国家有太多事情压在我的心头。周一晚上，在菲萨约·索扬博摄影展上，这种情绪更加沉重。我称他为“尼日利亚第一号亡命之徒记者”。他曾秘密潜入非法移民队伍，假扮一名渴望经由利比亚前往意大利的移民。他在路上奔波了47天，从尼日利亚卡诺的出发地出发，一路前往利比亚的黎波里，贩运分子通常会在那里抛弃他们的“客户”。他讲述了一个令人痛心不已的故事，其中充满非人化虐待、强奸和死亡。他抵达黎波里后结束了旅程，带回大量照片，鲜明地讲述了这个悲惨的故事。

索扬博提出了若干深刻观点。第一，移民 themselves 本身就是受害者。许多人正在尼日利亚严峻的经济压力下苦苦挣扎。我们不能因为他们寻求更好的生活而责怪他们。贩运分子向他们许诺天堂与尘世。即使在国内，许多尼日利亚人每天也会离开村庄前往拉各斯和阿布贾，因为那里似乎 promising 更好的生活。因此，我们很难因为尼日利亚人展望欧洲、追求更好的生活而责怪他们。移民，如果安排得当，并不是一种罪过。自创世以来，人类就一直出于经济原因离开故土。问题不在于离开的愿望，而在于致命且非法的路线，以及从中获利的贩运分子。

第二，索扬博说，打算成为非正规移民的人并非不知道危险，但他们总希望自己的遭遇会有所不同。对他们而言，留在尼日利亚并不是一个选择。他们的决心，堪比《圣经》中所讲的四个麻风病人。叙利亚士兵围困撒马利亚后，他们坐在城外；面对饿死的必然命运，他们自问：“我们为什么要坐在这里等死？如果我们说‘让我们进城去’，我们会因城中的饥荒而死；但如果坐在这里，我们同样会死。”于是他们决定向叙利亚人投降，说：“如果他们杀了我们，那我们就死了。”这也与以斯帖所说的“我若死，就死吧”如出一辙。

说实话，对那些不惜一切手段出国寻找新天地的人指指点点，对我而言很容易，但我没有身处他们的境地。我生活得相对安稳。我是一名雇主，能够养活自己和家人，也能出国度假。但数百万尼日利亚人都在勉强糊口。他们面对的现实与我截然不同。他们每天醒来都希望生活会好起来，但许多人往往饥饿而绝望地睡去。他们极易受到黄金国的诱惑，为到达那里什么都愿意做。我们可以质疑这些非正规移民的判断，却不能淡化他们的绝望与困顿。身处其中的人，才会真正明白那是什么感受。

我们观看完他在47天秘密旅程中拍摄的47张照片后，索扬博回答了来宾的提问。他说，自其关于亲身经历的三部分报道发表以来，没有任何政府机构与他联系过，甚至连派人向他了解有助于追查人口贩运分子的信息都没有。出发点位于卡诺，那里有明确的实体地址，有充当接头人的线人，有协助偷渡的安排人员，也牵涉到银行账户信息。至少五家政府机构的职责在不同程度上包括打击人口贩运。也许他们正在自行调查，但与一名“参与式观察者”交谈又有什么损失呢？

那天晚上我-bed时感到沮丧失落，因为这样一项意义重大的新闻作品，未能得到有关当局的重视。除了帮助追查贩运分子外，它还是极佳的材料，可以警示那些执意踏上通往欧洲的跨撒哈拉路线的人。索扬博透露，许多踏上这段旅程的人最终都追悔莫及。我立刻想到，这对开展宣传和引导大有用途。难道当局已经疲于追查线索？难道他们没有从索扬博的报道中看到任何有价值的东西？又或者，他们错过了这篇报道，尽管他们都有负责媒体监测的公共传播部门？

尼日利亚领导层的许多问题都令我忧虑，这次也不例外。报道称 gospel 歌手奥拉耶米·巴约尼莱·博拉吉去世，更广为人知的名字是Toluwanisings，这令我心情沉重。他的助手称，他突发紧急状况，却遭到“七、八家医院”拒收。在尼日利亚，许多急症患者被冷酷地拒绝接受救命的治疗，最终在极其悲惨的情况下死去。这种事一直在发生。别忘了，我们有法律禁止拒收急症患者，更不用说医学伦理以及《希波克拉底誓言》的精神了。但尼日利亚已经变成了这样。这也是许多人对生活失去希望的原因之一。

供电状况也令我心情沉重。尽管电力部长约瑟夫·特格贝荒唐声称，一些用电客户还要求他让电力供应“显著改善”的脚步“慢一点”，理由是冰箱里的物品都结冰了，但许多地方的供电状况依然糟糕透顶。如果那是个玩笑，那这个玩笑实在品味极差，简直麻木不仁。企业每年要花数十亿买汽油和柴油，这对尼日利亚联邦共和国的一位部长而言竟是个玩笑？我绝不建议拿一件正在摧毁尼日利亚人生计的事开玩笑。这进一步暴露了尼日利亚领导层的品格。我们本可以做得更好。

尼日利亚的领导层总有些东西暴露出专注力和同理心的缺失。我们对此已经习以为常。再看看自1999年转向民主以来的供电状况。如果有认真的领导，到如今全国本都可以享有不间断的电力供应——即使我们是从零开始，当时连电缆和变压器都没有。这关乎目标一致和意志坚忍。这个世界上，任何事、任何人都无法让我相信，供电危机不可能在27年内解决。我们可以找遍全世界的所有借口，但最令人痛心的事实是：我们根本就是一群不认真的人。只能这样说。

当你把一切放在一起看——令人震惊的供电状况、不堪居住的医疗体系、同一国家民众的经济处境，而在这样的国家里，一位失业的青年领袖竟敢把全新的SUV当作礼物送人——你不可能不对尼日利亚领导层的敏感度感到惊讶。领导究竟对我们意味着什么？看着数千名尼日利亚人因绝望而离境，却几乎不做什么来给予他们希望？看着穷人在医院遭到驱赶，仅仅因为“没有床位”而被迫回家等死？看着到处都是垃圾堆，相关人士却飞往迪拜庆祝某位政治人物的60岁生日？

领导力体现在回应现实，但这个国家处处冷漠。有时我真想知道，在一个医疗中心运转不良、紧急服务几乎不存在、数千名学生没有化学试剂却在上化学课、许多学校没有图书馆或实验室的社会里，我们的领导者夜里如何安睡？身为地方议会主席或州长，你怎么能对坑洼和烂路视而不见？又怎么能对没有自来水的社区无动于衷？

所有这些领导失误都在剥夺普通公民的希望，并迫使许多人寻求穿越撒哈拉的解决方案。我的结论一直是我们迫切需要一种新的领导力——政府各层级、各机构都需要。我们需要一种新文化，需要一种专注、负责、敏感且能回应民意的领导文化。我们一直在讨论领导问题，却往往只关注能力。这当然是最根本的，但能力必须与同情心和专注力并存。我们必须抓住每一个机会，不断呼吁领导者的集体良知，不断提醒他们肩负着对公民的责任。不管谁掌权，改善人民生活都必须是领导工作的核心重点。

事实上，尼日利亚人的要求并不过分。他们想要的只是真正关心他们的领导者。问题在于，双方根本没有建立联系。领导者与公民之间的情感鸿沟太深。总统肩负着巨大的责任，州长、地方议会主席、部长和公共机构负责人同样如此。每一个人都必须为自己的职位职责作出交代。我们对良心的呼吁，必须有追究其责任的决心作为支撑。尼日利亚人民值得拥有愿意认真推动事情落实的领导者。不该有任何尼日利亚人绝望到把撒哈拉视为唯一的出路。让人民有理由相信自己的国家，是领导者的首要职责。

执政党APC总统竞选委员会发言人阿尔万·哈桑先生在接受ARISE采访时声称，部长们花费数十亿奈拉以谋取职位。如果我说这是第一次听到这项指控，那就是在撒谎。不过，我仍然惊讶，这项指控竟出自执政党的一名高层。APC全国宣传秘书费利克斯·莫尔卡先生迅速出面进行损害控制。他说，哈桑谈的是历届政府中的部长，而不是在蒂努布总统任内任职的部长。嗯。让曾在布哈里、乔纳森和奥巴桑乔总统任内任职的部长们站出来说话，不是很好吗？太令人失望了。

独立国家选举委员会（INEC）开展的选民登记因发现疑似人工智能生成的图像而陷入风波。我不是技术专家，因此在这方面能作出的评论可能有限。但如果一名选民是到场接受身份核验登记的，图像怎么可能由人工智能生成，除非其中有什么蹊跷？我原以为，是一些在线登记的人上传了人工智能生成的图像，但INEC表示已经查出幕后相关人员。清理登记名册是一项艰巨任务。委员会通常会公示名册供公众提出意见。最终名册公布时，我们有责任密切监督。要保持警惕。

反对派的竞选操盘手难道还比得上“教授”泰沃·奥耶德莱，也就是财政部长吗？这位税务专家几乎每天都为反对派制作针对蒂努布总统的竞选材料。他最近表示，燃油税将在“经济稳定后”开征，随后又自作聪明地给相关报道贴上“假新闻”的标签——可他本人发布的视频恰恰证实他确实说过这番话。他又失言了，说有些家庭把收入的120%花在食物上。他总是搬起石头砸自己的脚，我原以为当上部长多少能帮到他。他显然很享受自己说话的声音。这种人真是让人无法可救，无药可救。

在我看来，为应对阿提库·阿布巴卡以经济困境为重点的竞选策略，蒂努布政府已批准向公务员发放每月N70,000的交通补贴，为期6个月。但尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）称这份纾困方案力度不足，转而要求立即把最低工资者的基本工资提高到N300,000。事实上，工会已经拒绝了N70,000的纾困方案。我当时不明白，TUC为什么要拒绝一份自己并未参与谈判的奖金？无论如何，如果我每月收入N70,000，又有人额外提供N70,000交通补贴，我为什么应该拒绝？真是不可思议。

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026110102.body_zh: （首尔=韩联社）记者柳美娜=美国总统唐纳德·特朗普再次威胁要重新发动袭击，称伊朗仍有“一两处”需要“处理”的目标。据法新社等媒体报道，特朗普总统31日（当地时间）在佛罗里达州马里兰的私人住所与记者会面时表示，美国已经使伊朗相当一部分军事力量失去作战能力，但“一两处仍需要处理，10分钟就能办到”。特朗普总统还提到了被称为伊朗主要地下核设施的“镐山”（Pickaxe Mountain），称其是需要“处理”的地点，并补充说：“我们很快就能处理掉。”这些表态出现在特朗普总统第二任期临近中期选举、选举日仅剩三天之际，有关“选举之后”打击伊朗的传闻不断升温之际。谈及由调解国参与的伊朗谈判，特朗普总统表示：“进展顺利”，但同时说：“他们不太值得信任”“我们会看看能否达成协议”。这番言论紧随国务卿马可·鲁比奥在G20外长会议前表示，特朗普总统尚未决定是否再次袭击伊朗，并倾向于通过外交途径解决之后。韩国《Money Today》此前也报道称，特朗普政府已通知海湾盟国，要为中期选举次日、即4日可能发生的空袭做好准备。伊朗正处于预告强硬回应的状态。伊朗最高领袖阿亚图拉赛耶德·穆查巴·哈梅内伊当天向军队下达指示：“无论威胁达到何种程度、属于何种类型，都必须以即时而有力、不受地域限制的回应加以应对。”稿件及图片转载授权：KakaoTalk okjebo <版权所有(c) 韩联社，未经许可禁止转载、再发布及用于人工智能训练和利用> 2026年11月1日11时17分发布

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/f.summary_zh: “他当时就在房间里。”桑沃-奥卢在谈及新冠肺炎疫情、2020年10月的艰难事件、重大基础设施决策，以及每当州长不在时哈姆扎特所承担的责任时，反复强调了这句话。值得注意的是，桑沃-奥卢亲自鼓励居民阅读该宣言，审视其内容，并将拟议政策与他们所在街区、市场和子女就读的学校联系起来。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/f.body: The unveiling of a governorship manifesto is ordinarily an occasion for political promises, ceremonial endorsements and the presentation of a candidate’s vision. But the October 30, 2026, event at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, acquired an additional dimension through Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s address. By the time the governor concluded his speech, the occasion had moved beyond the presentation of Dr. Obafemi Hamzat’s development agenda. It had also become a statement about political succession, institutional continuity and the arguments the All Progressives Congress (APC) intends to take into the 2027 governorship contest. What made the speech particularly interesting was its structure. Sanwo-Olu did not begin by cataloguing the achievements of his administration or appealing for support for his deputy. He began with history. He revisited the 2018 APC governorship contest, recalled Hamzat’s withdrawal in his favour and proceeded to offer an account of their seven years of governing together. The recollections established the foundation for the central argument he subsequently developed: that Hamzat’s candidature should be examined in the context of his long participation in the governance of Lagos. It was an argument built around a memorable expression. “He was in the room.” Sanwo-Olu repeated the words while discussing the COVID-19 pandemic, the difficult events of October 2020, major infrastructure decisions and the responsibilities undertaken by Hamzat whenever the governor was away. The expression served as a narrative device connecting separate historical episodes. It also allowed the governor to present the candidate’s experience as something more personal than a collection of appointments in a political biography. The campaign theme, “Lagos… Forward Together,” consequently acquired a particular interpretation through the governor’s speech. For Sanwo-Olu, moving forward was not presented as a rejection of the past but as an attempt to build on existing institutions, programmes and projects while addressing outstanding problems. That was also the significance of his relay-race analogy. He traced a succession of administrations from Bola Tinubu in 1999 through Babatunde Fashola, Akinwunmi Ambode and his own government, arguing that each transition had drawn upon varying degrees of experience accumulated in earlier administrations. The metaphor offered a historical explanation for APC’s preference for continuity in Lagos. It also gave the governor an opportunity to introduce a more contentious argument: whether extensive familiarity with an existing system should be preferred to an alternative approach to governance. His declaration that Lagos does not hand the baton to a man standing still was the central expression of that position. But the metaphor has its limitations. Experience within government can provide institutional knowledge and familiarity with administrative processes. It can also encourage the preservation of practices that may require reform. The test is therefore not merely how long a candidate has participated in a system, but what that participation has produced and how the candidate proposes to address its deficiencies. Sanwo-Olu partly anticipated this question by distinguishing consolidation from stagnation. He explained that continuity should involve completing existing work, correcting what is not functioning properly and initiating the next phase of development. That qualification is important because it connects the political case for succession to the practical content of Hamzat’s manifesto. Titled: “The Lagos Promise,” the document contains 100 pledges organised under seven pillars represented by the acronym PROMISE: People First, Renewal, Opportunity, Machinery of Government, Inclusion, Security and Resilience, and Everyday Dignity. Among the proposals announced at the event were commitments concerning public transportation, affordable housing, healthcare facilities, child protection, environmental services and the management of government. Those pledges provide a measurable basis for assessing the campaign’s claims. Lagosians can ask what the proposals will cost, which institutions will implement them, how they will be financed and what timelines should govern delivery. It was significant that Sanwo-Olu himself encouraged residents to read the manifesto, interrogate its contents and relate the proposed policies to their streets, markets and children’s schools. In doing so, he acknowledged, at least rhetorically, that public acceptance should rest on more than the candidate’s familiarity with government. The same principle applies to the governor’s account of the past. His testimony establishes how he views his deputy’s contribution to the administration. It does not remove the electorate’s responsibility to examine that record independently. Indeed, one consequence of making Hamzat’s participation in past decisions central to the campaign is that the candidate’s association with the outgoing administration becomes a legitimate subject of public questioning. The achievements, policy controversies and unfinished obligations of the Sanwo-Olu years are all relevant to that examination. Yet the address was not solely a statement of policy and history. Its closing passages moved decisively into campaign organisation. Sanwo-Olu reminded APC members of the support Hamzat had received during the party’s nomination process and directed their attention beyond the internal contest. The message was that securing the party’s ticket was only the beginning of the larger electoral engagement. He urged the party to take its message across Ikeja, Ikorodu, Badagry, Epe and Lagos Island, reaching communities and voters throughout the state. The shift in emphasis was unmistakable. The governor had begun by telling the audience about rooms where decisions were made. He ended by directing the party towards the streets where the public would assess those decisions and the promises that followed. That transition captures the political significance of the entire occasion. Inside the manifesto hall, Sanwo-Olu could speak with the authority of a governor describing his own experience. Outside it, the arguments he presented will have to compete with the everyday realities of Lagos residents and the alternatives offered by other candidates. The campaign, therefore, enters its next phase with a clearly articulated theme but also a considerable burden of explanation. It must connect the historical record invoked by Sanwo-Olu with the practical expectations contained in Hamzat’s manifesto. It must demonstrate that continuity can accommodate reform, that institutional experience can produce measurable improvements and that political harmony within an administration translates into public value. More importantly, the APC will have to defend its record while explaining what Hamzat proposes to do differently. That is what gave Friday’s speech its campaign-opening character. Sanwo-Olu supplied the historical narrative, identified the administrative experience on which his deputy intends to rely and connected both to the manifesto’s future commitments. He also gave the party a political message that can now be examined in the wider public arena. The governing partnership has supplied its account of the past. The manifesto has set out commitments for the future. Between those two lies the campaign itself, where the decisive questions will concern performance, credibility, delivery and the interests of the people of Lagos. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/f.title_zh: 从房间到街头：桑沃-奥卢如何为哈姆扎特的竞选造势
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/f.body_zh: 州长竞选宣言的发布通常是一次作出政治承诺、进行仪式性背书和展示候选人愿景的场合。然而，2026年10月30日，在拉各斯伊甘穆的沃雷·索因卡文化与创意艺术中心举行的这次活动，通过州长巴巴吉德·桑沃-奥卢的讲话获得了另一层意义。州长结束演讲时，这场活动已经超越了展示奥巴费米·哈姆扎特博士发展议程的范畴，也成为对政治权力交接、机构延续性以及全进步大会党打算在2027年州长选举中提出的论点的声明。这篇讲话尤其引人之处在于其结构。桑沃-奥卢没有从列举其政府的政绩开始，也没有为其副手争取支持，而是从历史谈起。他回顾了2018年全进步大会党州长选举，提到哈姆扎特为支持他而退出竞选，随后讲述了两人共同执政7年的经历。这些回忆为他随后展开的核心论点奠定了基础，即应结合哈姆扎特长期参与拉各斯治理的情况来审视其候选人资格。这一论点围绕一句令人难忘的话展开：“他当时就在那个房间里。”桑沃-奥卢在谈及新冠疫情、2020年10月的困难事件、重大基础设施决策，以及每当州长不在时哈姆扎特所承担的责任时，反复提及这句话。这句话成为连接不同历史片段的叙事手段，也让州长得以将候选人的经验呈现为比政治履历中一系列职务任命更具个人色彩的历练。因此，竞选主题“拉各斯……携手向前”经由州长的讲话获得了特定诠释。在桑沃-奥卢看来，向前并不意味着否定过去，而是意味着在解决遗留问题的同时，以现有机构、方案和项目为基础继续建设。这正是他采用接力赛比喻的意义所在。他追溯了从1999年博拉·蒂努布，到巴巴通德·法绍拉、阿金温米·阿姆博德，再到其本人政府的历届政府，主张每一次权力交接都借鉴了前几届政府积累的不同程度的经验。这一比喻为全进步大会党偏好拉各斯政策延续性提供了历史解释，也给了州长引入一个更具争议性论点的机会：与采取另一种治理方式相比，对现有体系的广泛熟悉是否应当更受青睐。他宣称拉各斯不会把接力棒交给一个原地踏步的人，这正是这一立场的集中体现。不过，这一比喻也有其局限。 政府任职经历能够带来机构知识和对行政流程的熟悉，也可能助长对那些需要改革的做法的保留。因此，考验候选人的不仅是其参与某个体系的时间长短，还有这种参与取得了什么成果，以及候选人打算如何解决其中的不足。桑沃-奥卢预先部分回应了这一问题，将巩固与停滞区分开来。他解释说，延续应当意味着完成现有工作、纠正运转不当的环节，并启动发展的下一阶段。这一限定很重要，因为它将主张权力交接的政治理由与哈姆扎特宣言的实际内容联系起来。这份题为《拉各斯承诺》的文件包含100项承诺，按七大支柱组织，以PROMISE这一缩写表示，即人民优先、更新、机遇、政府机制、包容、安全与韧性，以及日常尊严。活动中公布的建议包括有关公共交通、经济适用住房、医疗设施、儿童保护、环境服务以及政府管理的承诺。这些承诺为评估竞选团队的各项主张提供了可衡量的依据。拉各斯居民可以追问这些建议需要多少成本、哪些机构负责执行、资金从何而来，以及交付应遵循什么时间表。值得注意的是，桑沃-奥卢亲自鼓励居民阅读宣言、审视其内容，并将拟议政策与他们街道上的现实、市场状况和子女就读的学校联系起来。借此，他至少在言辞上承认，公众的接受不能仅建立在候选人熟悉政府运作这一点上。同一原则也适用于州长对过去的叙述。他的证词说明了他如何看待副手对本届政府的贡献，却没有免除选民独立审查这段经历的责任。事实上，将哈姆扎特参与过往决策作为竞选核心所产生的一个结果，是候选人与即将卸任的政府之间的关联成为可以公开质询的正当议题。桑沃-奥卢任期内的政绩、政策争议和未履行的义务，都与这一审查相关。然而，这篇讲话并非仅仅是对政策和历史的陈述。其结尾部分明确转向竞选组织工作。桑沃-奥卢提醒全进步大会党成员，哈姆扎特在党内提名过程中获得了广泛支持，并要求他们把目光投向党内竞争之外。其传达的信息是，取得党内候选人提名只是更广泛选举活动。他说，赢得党内提名只是更大范围选举争取的开始。他敦促该党在伊凯贾、伊科罗杜、巴达格里、埃佩和拉各斯岛传达其竞选信息，触达全州各地的社区和选民。重心的转变十分明确。州长起初向听众讲述决策所在的房间，结束时则引导该党走向街头，让公众在那里评估这些决策以及此后的承诺。这一转变概括了整场活动的政治意义。在宣言发布大厅内，桑沃-奥卢可以凭借州长身份，以讲述自身经历的权威发言；在大厅之外，他提出的论点必须与拉各斯居民的日常现实以及其他候选人提出的替代方案展开竞争。因此，这次竞选进入下一阶段时，不仅有了清晰阐述的主题，也背负着相当重的解释负担。它必须把桑沃-奥卢所援引的历史记录与哈姆扎特宣言所包含的实际期望联系起来，必须证明延续性能够容纳改革、机构经验能够带来可衡量的改善，而且政府内部的政治协调能够转化为公共价值。更重要的是，全进步大会党必须为自身任期内的记录辩护，同时说明哈姆扎特打算采取哪些不同做法。正是这些内容使周五的讲话具有竞选开场的性质。桑沃-奥卢提供了历史叙事，指明其副手准备依靠的行政经验，并将二者与宣言对未来作出的承诺联系起来。他还向该党传达了一条可以在更广泛的公共领域加以审视的政治信息。执政搭档已经讲述了过去的经历，宣言则提出了对未来的承诺，而两者之间就是竞选本身，其中的决定性问题将涉及施政表现、可信度、承诺兑现以及拉各斯人民的利益。THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/e.summary_zh: 加冕盛典最辉煌的一幕出现在正式加冕日，来自远近各地的受邀嘉宾陆续抵达奥波博镇，被引导进入贾贾国王宫殿的场地，现场沿线搭起了色彩绚丽、品味雅致的华盖。按日计划举行的加冕典礼活动很快进入尾声：国王加冕感恩礼拜于2026年9月27日星期日在奥波博卡莱阿比亚马镇的圣马可（圣公会）教堂举行。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/01/e.body: It was the culmination of activities heralding a milestone event which attracted a galaxy of dignitaries which included foremost traditional rulers, a former President of Nigeria and many political leaders, captains of industry and well wishes from across the length and breadth of this great country. It is recalled that the 67-year-old monarch was proclaimed as King-designate December 13, 2025 to succeed his late elder brother, King Dandeson Douglas Jaja; Jeki V, who had passed in April, 2025. However and unexpectedly, a form of dissension and threat of a legal challenge to the process of his emergence arose but was mercifully and expertly put down in an admirable and lawful manner two and half months after on March 16, 2026. It was indeed a showtime of the rich Ibani Cultural heritage, rites and aquatic displays of ceremonial gigs of the various war Canoe houses on the Opobo river including King JaJa’s war canoe itself – personally commanded by the King-designate. His appearances at the various cultural display grounds were significant moments during which he acknowledged the joyous and thunderous greetings from the participants and equally extended affectionate gestures to them, the people and to the drummers who sounded the throne’s drum name in ceaseless adulations. The crowning glory came on the coronation day proper as invited guests from far and near arrived Opobo Town and were ushered into King JaJa’s Palace ground that was lined up with colourfully and tastefully decorated canopies. Top-most VIPs were shaded in the canopies pitched directly opposite the coronation dias for obvious reasons. The dias itself dressed in red and velvet colours was a slightly elevated platform on which a gold trimmed royal throne for the King was placed. In the front row of these VIP canopies sat great personages of power and influence in our society which included former President Goodluck Jonathan and former First Lady, Dame Patience Jonathan. To their immediate right sat the ever adorable King Edward Ashimini William Dappa Pepple III, Perekule XI and Amanyanabo of Grand Bonny Kingdom, who arrived the venue escorted by a 28-man fully-clad Otobo Masquerades Squad. It is rare to see Grand Bonny’s Monarch appear in a public event in practical demonstration of the metaphorical symbol of his majestic and towering strength – traditionally reserved for the King to honour another royal as it was on that day. The Otobo masquerade is believed to represent the hippopotamus (that amphibious power house often called the river horse – due largely to its enormous strength and fearsomeness on land and at sea). Other notable royals who graced the occasion were the Obong of Calabar, the Obi of Onitsha, King Asari Dokubo of Elem Kalabari, King Winston Alamina-Oputebeya of Koniama in Okrika, the traditional rulers from Ahoada and other members of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers as well as a host of many other invited political big wigs and captains of industry. The crowd of visitors and locals was impressive and almost made the venue chaotic, leaving the security details of these VIPs literally cueless regarding how to keep their principals safe and far from possible harm which never happened anyway. Then came the coronation address which the king read with a calm and dignified voice – acknowledging each and every important dignitary present – beginning with former President Jonathan and his dear wife and then the Amanayabo of Grand Bonny whom he addressed as ‘‘his brother and King of our ancestral home’’. A truly noble and pristine appellation intended to unmistakably strike the cord of consanguinity amongst the Ibani people of both kingdoms present at the event or elsewhere. The king in his address – acknowledged the weight of the Crown placed on his head and the enormous responsibilities of his office and the throne whose dignity and integrity he vowed to uphold. He also pledged to keep the trust bestowed upon him with a promise to invest and promote the development of his kingdom and people. In his address, he displayed a rare emotional connection with the legitimate expectations of Opobians by including the development of cultural centers that would incorporate the Ibani language into everyday domestic usages – as part of his coronation charter with his people. This is a huge and necessary project in order to reverse the unhappy but steady decline in use of Ibani language amongst our people. He promised to make his reign and Opobo Kingdom a dependable stakeholder in pursuit of peace, development and unity of Rovers State and by extension Nigeria as a whole. At the end of his speech, came a deluge of tributes offered as homage by the former president, Obi of Onitsha and other royals. King Charles Douglas MacPepple JaJa; Jeki VI is truly a monarch in whom his people rejoices for so many reasons: Born on January 27, 1959 his primary education in Opobo Town and his secondary education in Akwa Ibom State before proceeding to the University of Port Harcourt where he earned his bachelor degree. His professional and social lives were marked by steady progression through SPDC to the Nigerian Bulk Oil Company and others. He join Mina Ogbo King Cultural Society of Opobo at the age of 12 – which speaks to his avid love for cultural and traditional activities and overtime acquired drumming skills and mastery in the rhythmical handling of local musical instruments and talking – drums to the amazement of local folks – earning him the Sobriquet of ‘‘akwa-alabo’’ (Lord of the drums). A truly home breed royal and man of the people. Furthermore, he became Chairman of Chief MacPepple War Canoe House PH branch – between 1989-1998, the Alapalibo (Deputy Chief) of that house in 2006, the Alabo-designate (Chief designate) in 2008 and finally became the Alabo (Chief) of that house in 2009 – a position he held until his proclamation and eventual coronation as King a month ago. His life trajectories and pedigree is rich and ennobling enough to have endeared him to all Strata of Opobo Society and immensely certifies him as a proverbial ‘‘square peg in a square hole’’. The closing chapter to the daily planned Coronation activities came in quick succession with the King’s Coronation Thanksgiving Service held at St Mark’s (Anglican Communion) Church in Kalaibiama Town – Opobo on Sunday, September 27, 2026. The King, the royal family, the Alapu, title citizens and well-wishers were in full attendance amidst a heavy down pour which contrasted with the fine weather of the previous-day of the Coronation proper – which many believed were showers of blessing from above upon the Monarch and Opobo Kingdom. In all, it would be very apposite to say that the coronation was very successful and well organized by the event planners and the various committees who worked assiduously to produce this commendable outcome.
